title: Google says it fixed more Chrome bugs in June than over the past two years, thanks to AI
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: As experts have warned for the last two years, some companies — like Microsoft and now Google — are finding and patching an exponential number of bugs in their products, thanks to ...
body:
Google has announced a significant leap in browser security, attributing a record number of Chrome bug fixes to its internal AI tools. In June alone, the company patched an impressive 1,072 security vulnerabilities across the last two Chrome versions, a figure that surpasses the total number of fixes implemented over the previous two years combined (1,036 bugs across 23 versions). This unprecedented acceleration in vulnerability resolution highlights a transformative shift in cybersecurity, mirroring similar AI-driven advancements reported by Microsoft.

This dramatic increase in security patches is powered by advanced AI models, including Google's Gemini. These Large Language Models (LLMs) are fundamentally reshaping the economics of cybersecurity by automating the process of vulnerability discovery and transforming it into an industrial-scale operation. By leveraging AI, Google can now proactively identify and address security flaws, effectively staying ahead of malicious actors and continuously enhancing Chrome's safety with every update.

For developers and researchers, this development carries profound implications. It validates earlier predictions regarding AI's potential to exponentially accelerate bug identification, underscoring the necessity for security teams to integrate AI into their defensive strategies. This shift promises a future of more robust and secure software platforms, where AI plays a crucial role in building safer applications from the ground up. Researchers, in turn, gain valuable insights into the practical, large-scale deployment of AI for proactive security, opening new avenues for exploring AI's role in automated threat detection, vulnerability patching, and fostering a more secure digital ecosystem.
